doc.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Harmonica, banjo and teaching himself guitar
summary: Ellis played harmonica at three and banjo at seven, then outdid his older brother on a guitar using a Sears Roebuck instruction book.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Oh, let me see. Well I first played the harmonica when I was three, so I’m told, and it must be true ‘cause I can still play it a little bit, very little. And then my parents bought me a banjo when I was seven. And I learned to play that, and then somebody left a guitar at our house, and my older brother wanted to accompany me. So he’d tune the guitar incorrectly, you know. It would be hard to show you, but well it was a cheap shot. You’d connect the chords with just one finger, see? And so being an older brother he did everything much better than I did. So I saw that I had him, so I got a book from Sears Roebuck that said, “Learn to play the guitar in five minutes,” and I believed it. So I learned to play it correctly and I showed him how to play, and so that was a good lift for me.
